blog/en/glucose-meter-at-home-brain-heal.title: Brain health in one drop of blood
panels: When blood sugar swings widely, the brain tires along with it.
Blood sugar and brain are linked
As the link between blood sugar and brain health becomes known, more people are measuring.
Wash your hands, dry them well, then measure. Two or three times a week is enough.
See a doctor if 126 mg/dL or higher repeats. Day to day, eat vegetables and protein first.

blog/en/normal-blood-sugar-but-an-aging-.title: Normal blood sugar, aging brain?
panels: But my blood sugar is normal?
Even without a diabetes diagnosis, some signs mean you can't relax.
Insulin resistance dulls the brain, especially the hippocampus, which is why it's called "type 3 diabetes."
Walking alone may not be enough. Add strength training and balance exercises.
If you notice heavy sleepiness and fatigue after meals or a growing waistline, see a doctor.

blog/en/why-resolutions-keep-lasting-thr.title: Reading that builds the aMCC
panels: Gave up on day three again
When resolutions keep fizzling out, we blame our weak willpower.
The aMCC (anterior midcingulate cortex), just inside the frontal lobe, is tied to willpower and focus.
Pushing past reluctance with reading at the same time every day trains the aMCC.
Even a few minutes of consistency grows the circuit.

blog/en/what-is-the-carnivore-diet-peopl.title: What is the carnivore diet?
panels: Many people say their focus clouds over after carb-heavy meals.
Cutting carbs is said to make ketone bodies the brain's fuel and stimulate BDNF.
Shift slowly toward animal foods, and be sure to get enough water and electrolytes.
Some reviews report benefits, but if you have a condition, talk to an expert first.

blog/en/three-day-resolutions-use-bdnf-a.title: Beat three-day resolutions with BDNF and the aMCC
panels: When plans don't last three days, it's easy to blame a weak-willed personality.
Brain fertilizer and a willpower button
BDNF is the brain's fertilizer; the aMCC is the willpower button that pushes through what you'd rather not do.
Instead of grand plans, finishing one small discomfort today wakes up both.
Overdoing it backfires. Consistency grows intelligence and willpower together.

blog/en/flat-feet-high-arches-normal-arc.title: Running shoes for your foot arch
panels: If your knees or soles hurt every time you run, look at your feet before your shoes.
The foot arch absorbs landing shock. Flat feet and high arches need different shoes.
Stability for flat, cushion for high
Flat feet: stability shoes that control overpronation. High arches: maximal cushion.
Trying shoes on in the afternoon or evening, when feet swell slightly, means fewer bad buys.

blog/en/running-for-brain-health-beginne.title: For beginner runners with sore knees
panels: Many people start running and stop within days because of knee and shin pain.
The foot arch absorbs shock, and shoes that don't match your arch type add strain.
Check your arch type at home and choose running shoes to match.
Running steadily without pain keeps the BDNF and mood benefits coming.

blog/en/bdnf-just-10-minutes-of-running-.title: How 10 minutes of running changes the brain
panels: Often it's the brain that tires before the body. Memory and mood sink together.
Running wakes up BDNF, the "brain fertilizer" that grows and connects brain cells.
At a talking pace, like slow jogging, starting with 10 minutes is plenty.
Run steadily and learning and memory sharpen, and stress shakes you less.

blog/en/what-does-insulin-do-and-how-to-.title: How to use insulin wisely
panels: You've heard that eating lots of refined carbs makes you gain weight easily, right?
Insulin keeps blood sugar steady, but too much of it invites fat storage.
Change your eating order, take a 15-minute walk after meals, and cut back on snacks.
Lower-body strength training and skipping refined carbs on an empty morning stomach steady blood sugar.

blog/en/what-to-eat-right-before-a-big-d.title: What to eat right before a big day
panels: When an important task doesn't go as hoped, negative thoughts start to loop.
On tense days, the brain burns through a lot of energy and runs low fast.
Cacao chocolate gives you strength faster than nuts, which take a long time to digest.
Failure is the default, success a bonus
What you eat supports your focus and resilience.

blog/en/which-foods-are-rich-in-bdnf.title: A table that supports BDNF
panels: Sometimes it's hard to know what to eat for your brain.
BDNF affects the survival and plasticity of nerve cells.
Even one brain-minded meal a day supports the hippocampus.

blog/en/what-causes-bdnf-deficiency-and-.title: Three reasons BDNF drops
panels: Chronic stress is the number one thing that eats away at the brain's BDNF.
Lack of exercise and a diet high in fructose lower BDNF too.
High-intensity aerobic exercise raises blood BDNF levels even more.
The brain comes back to life
When BDNF recovers, mood and focus revive along with serotonin.

blog/en/bdnf-brain-derived-neurotrophic-.title: BDNF, what are you?
panels: When stress and binge eating go on, both body and mind grow heavy.
BDNF is a neurotrophic factor that grows nerve cells and supports learning and memory.
BDNF raises resilience, helping you get back up when you fall.

blog/en/intermittent-fasting-a-secret-fo.title: Intermittent fasting after the holidays
panels: Over the holidays you eat at all hours, and the body never gets a break.
During fasting hours, ketosis and autophagy kick in and insulin sensitivity improves.
Set your eating window and chew well, eating vegetables → protein → carbs.
Body fat drops and BDNF rises, which also helps cognitive function.

blog/en/three-ways-to-achieve-your-goals.title: Three ways to reach your goals
panels: All I did was buy a diary…
You set New Year's goals, but your plans move more slowly than you'd hoped.
Think you already have it instead of what you lack, and impatience fades and starting gets easier.
Trust neuroplasticity, repeat small actions, and wake up the brain with exercise.
The hippocampus and frontal lobe wake up, and action follows.

blog/en/memory-is-less-true-so-write-it-.title: Memory is less true than we think
panels: I'm sure that's how it was…
We believe memory is as accurate as a photo, but in reality it often changes.
Each time the hippocampus and prefrontal cortex retrieve a memory, recall itself revises it.
Recording the day's facts and feelings gives you a steady reference point.
You get to know yourself better
Emotion strengthens memory. A record becomes a map for understanding yourself.

blog/en/lifelong-connectivity-neuroplast.title: A brain that changes for life
panels: People say brain function declines step by step as we age.
Neuroplasticity: the brain strengthens, restores and can rewire itself to a degree.
Medical students preparing for exams grew gray matter and the posterior hippocampus.
Emotional regulation, empathy and mindfulness help integrate the brain.

blog/en/wake-up-your-neuroplasticity.title: Wake up your neuroplasticity
panels: People say our heads stiffen with age, but the brain changes throughout life.
The core of neuroplasticity is adding nerve cells and strengthening synaptic networks.
The gut supports serotonin; deep sleep supports melatonin and recovery.
New information, laughter and happy experiences wake up the hippocampus and frontal lobe.

blog/en/is-the-placebo-effect-real.title: The placebo is real
panels: The stronger the pain, the easier it is to think the body is badly damaged.
Pain isn't an exact measure of damage; it's the brain's response to protect the body.
The sham-surgery group had less pain. Expectation and hope move the brain.
A brain with hope instead of learned helplessness helps recovery.

blog/en/the-secret-of-success.title: Sculpting a successful brain
panels: If you rest with nothing but passive activities, the brain doesn't change.
Neuroplasticity: the brain changes with intended actions and information. (Ramón y Cajal)
10 minutes of reading, blogging, 30 minutes of exercise, trying something new.
Put the same situation in good words, and the brain responds in that direction.

blog/en/the-brain-is-changing.title: The brain is changing
panels: Trying something new makes me sleepy
When you start something new, the brain "gifts" you sleep to protect the familiar way.
The brain tries to keep its established system, so resolutions easily come to nothing.
Instead of "What's wrong with me?", repeat small actions to cut a new path in the brain.
Using the brain you'll live with for life, you can now design a positive future.
